Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
игра
Wikipedia bg

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *jьgra.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [iˈɡra]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ra
  • Syllabification(key): и‧гра
  • Hyphenation(key): иг‧ра

Noun

[edit]

игра́ • (igrá) f (relational adjective игра́лен or игрови́, diminutive игри́ца or игри́чка)

  1. play, game (activity for amusement, entertainment, or sport)
    игра́ на кри́еница
    igrá na kríenica
    game of hide-and-seek
    игра́ на ка́рти
    igrá na kárti
    card game
  2. game, match, round (a single completed instance of such an activity)
    Загу́бих та́зи игра́.
    Zagúbih tázi igrá.
    I lost this game.
  3. play (the act or process of playing; manner of execution)
  4. game (a physical set of items used for a board game or similar activity)
  5. dance (usually a traditional folk dance; the act of dancing)
    Synonyms: танц (tanc), хоро́ (horó)
  6. acting, performance (execution of a role in theatre, film, etc.)
    Synonym: изпълне́ние (izpǎlnénie)
    Сюже́тът на фи́лма е интере́сен, но не ми харе́са игра́та на арти́стите.
    Sjužétǎt na fílma e interésen, no ne mi harésa igráta na artístite.
    The plot of the film is interesting, but I didn't like the actors' performance.
  7. (figurative) play, flickering, shimmering (lively or rapid movement (e.g. of light, snow, waves))
    игра́ на светлината́
    igrá na svetlinatá
    play of light
  8. (figurative) game, scheme, machination (premeditated actions with a hidden goal)
    опа́сна игра́
    opásna igrá
    dangerous game
  9. (figurative) play (free and flexible intellectual or creative activity)
    игра́ на сло́вото
    igrá na slóvoto
    play on words
  10. playing, frivolity (careless or unserious treatment of something important)
    игра́ с живо́та и смъртта́
    igrá s živóta i smǎrttá
    playing with life and death
  11. (archaic) play, drama (theatrical work)
    Synonyms: пие́са (piésa), дра́ма (dráma)

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьgra.

Noun

[edit]

игра • (igra) f (plural игри)

  1. game
  2. dance

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьgrati, from *jьgra.

Verb

[edit]

игра • (igra) third-singular present, impf (perfective изигра or одигра)

  1. (ambitransitive) to play
  2. (ambitransitive) to dance

Russian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic игра (igra), from Proto-Slavic *jьgra.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɪˈɡra]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

игра́ • (igrá) f inan (genitive игры́, nominative plural и́гры, genitive plural игр, relational adjective иго́рный or игрово́й)

  1. game
    игра́ в мяч ― igrá v mjač ― ball game
  2. a sport which is played (also спорти́вная игра́ (sportívnaja igrá))
  3. (action): play in the following senses:
    1. Activity for amusement only, especially among the young.
    2. Similar activity, in young animals, as they explore their environment and learn new skills.
    3. (ethology) "Repeated, incompletely functional behavior differing from more serious versions ..., and initiated voluntarily when ... in a low-stress setting."
    4. An individual's performance in a sport or game.
  4. acting, performance
    игра́ актёра ― igrá aktjóra ― an actor’s performance
  5. role-playing (also ролева́я игра́ (rolevája igrá))
  6. playing (a musical instrument)
    игра́ на гита́ре ― igrá na gitáre ― playing the guitar
  7. movement of gas bubbles in a sparkling drink
  8. (figuratively) glitter, sparkle, radiance (of precious stones)
